notes: Source of truth for product outcomes. Numeric KPIs are placeholders until validated against real telemetry / billing data. The ProductManager agent is forbidden from inventing values.

goals.title: Become a true multi-tenant platform
goals.description: Serve three audiences — Platform Operator, Client, and Customer (sub-tenant) — with strict tenant isolation and branded portals.

goals.title: Plugin-driven multi-device platform
goals.description: Decouple business logic from vendor transport so new GPS and fueling devices can be onboarded as plugins under FMS.Devices.*.

goals.title: Kenya fiscal compliance, region-ready architecture
goals.description: Achieve full KRA eTIMS (OSCU + VSCU) compliance with a provider model ready for additional fiscal regions.

goals.title: Unified M365 Fluent UX and permission model
goals.description: Standardize Microsoft 365 Admin Center design language and a single permission model across every frontend and every API.

kpis.name: Monthly Active Users
kpis.description: Distinct users with at least one authenticated session in the calendar month.

kpis.name: Feature Adoption Rate
kpis.description: Percentage of active tenants using at least one of: Vehicle Tracking, Fueling, Tank Stock, Task & Trip Management.

kpis.name: Customer Retention
kpis.description: Percentage of paying tenants retained quarter-over-quarter.

kpis.name: Monthly Recurring Revenue
kpis.description: Subscription revenue normalised to monthly basis (KES).

kpis.name: Net Promoter Score
kpis.description: Quarterly NPS survey of fleet managers and operators.

userStories.iWant: to add a new GPS tracking provider to my tenant without code changes
userStories.soThat: I can switch vendors or onboard new hardware as the business grows
acceptanceCriteria: Given a platform operator with a valid vendor licence, when they add a provider config in the Admin UI, then the new provider becomes selectable per vehicle.
Given a vehicle bound to the new provider, when a position is received, then it is persisted and visible on the live map within 5 seconds.

userStories.iWant: to onboard a new fueling device vendor as a plugin
userStories.soThat: we can support new pumps or ATGs without redeploying core services
acceptanceCriteria: Given a new vendor plugin DLL under FMS.Devices.Fueling/Providers/<Vendor>/, when the host restarts, then the provider auto-registers via [Provider] attribute scanning.
Given a tenant with the new provider configured, when a fueling transaction is received, then it persists with TenantId set and triggers the canonical MediatR notification.

userStories.iWant: vehicle positions to keep flowing if one tracking provider fails
userStories.soThat: operations are not interrupted by upstream vendor outages
acceptanceCriteria: Given two providers are configured for a tenant, when one provider's health check fails, then the ProviderHealthMonitor logs a warning and the other provider continues normally.
Given a provider returns errors for 3 consecutive minutes, when status is queried, then it is shown as 'degraded' in the admin dashboard.

userStories.iWant: to provision a new client tenant in a single screen
userStories.soThat: onboarding takes minutes instead of days
acceptanceCriteria: Given valid tenant details, when I submit the provisioning form, then a Tenant row, default admin user, and audience-scoped branding are created in one transaction.
Given the tenant is created, when the new admin opens the welcome email link, then they log in to a working portal with no further setup.

userStories.iWant: to create sub-customer tenants under my account
userStories.soThat: I can resell FMS to my own customers
acceptanceCriteria: Given I am a Client tenant admin, when I create a sub-customer, then ParentTenantId is set to my tenant and the customer cannot see sibling customers' data.
Given I open cross-tenant reports, when I select 'All customers', then I see aggregated metrics across my customers only.

userStories.iWant: to log in to a branded portal showing only my fleet
userStories.soThat: I trust the experience belongs to my provider, not a generic platform
acceptanceCriteria: Given my client has uploaded a logo and chosen brand colours, when I log in, then the portal shows those brand assets in the header and login page.
Given I open any list (vehicles, sites, reports), when results render, then only my tenant's data appears (verified by tenant isolation tests).

userStories.iWant: every API and UI action gated by a single permission key
userStories.soThat: role assignments behave predictably across backend, frontend, and DB
acceptanceCriteria: Given a permission key exists in the permissions table, when it is used in a [Authorize] attribute or usePermissions hook, then both reference the exact same string (no casing or prefix drift).
Given a role is missing a permission, when the user calls the protected endpoint, then they receive 403 Forbidden and the UI hides the corresponding control.

userStories.iWant: a single source of truth for permission names that matches code, DB, and frontend
userStories.soThat: compliance reviews complete in hours instead of days
acceptanceCriteria: Given the PermissionAudit agent runs, when it scans controllers, frontend hooks, and the rolepermissions table, then it reports zero drift items.
Given a new controller action is added without a permission check, when CI runs, then the build fails with a clear error.

userStories.iWant: the operator portal to look and feel like the tenant app
userStories.soThat: I can move between them without re-learning the UI
acceptanceCriteria: Given a user has access to both portals, when they switch between fms.frontend and FMS.Admin, then header height, sidebar width, font, and primary color are pixel-identical.

userStories.iWant: a single consistent shell across every module
userStories.soThat: vehicles, fueling, and tank stock pages all share the same chrome
acceptanceCriteria: Given any feature page, when it loads, then it renders inside SideNavOuterToolbar with the standard header, side nav, and footer — no custom chrome.

userStories.iWant: the portal to show only the pages I'm allowed to see
userStories.soThat: admin and operations routes don't clutter my navigation
acceptanceCriteria: Given tenant_kind=customer in JWT, when I log in, then the side nav renders only the customer allowlist (Dashboard, Vehicles, Reports, Notifications, Profile).

userStories.asA: any user when an error occurs
userStories.iWant: a friendly recovery screen instead of a blank page
userStories.soThat: I can navigate away and report the issue
acceptanceCriteria: Given a render or runtime error, when the page crashes, then GlobalErrorBoundary shows the standard error card with Go Home + Report Issue actions and the error is auto-reported (throttled) to the backend.

userStories.asA: any user on a slow or failing API
userStories.iWant: a clear inline message and a retry option
userStories.soThat: I am not stuck on a spinner
acceptanceCriteria: Given an Axios error surfaced via the shared error-toast/empty-state helpers, when displayed, then the user sees a message with status code, friendly text, and a retry/reload action.

userStories.iWant: a documented layout contract and design tokens
userStories.soThat: new pages match the system without re-inventing chrome
acceptanceCriteria: Given a new page component, when I follow the m365-page-header plus content-card pattern documented in the PRD, then no design review changes are required.

userStories.iWant: one document that says which Inspinia tokens we keep vs. which M365 tokens override them
userStories.soThat: I can spec new screens without ambiguity
acceptanceCriteria: Given the Inspinia Inheritance Matrix in PRD §6, when a designer specs a new screen, then every token (color, spacing, font, control height) maps to a row in the matrix.
